title: Workspace pattern: resizable primary region, edge chevron panels, yielding panels, control rail; Phase 2 and 3 candidate amendments
summary: Add a workspace pattern: a primary region that stays primary and can be resized by the person, side panels that yield (shrink, drawer, stack) before it, choices stored as preferences rather than measurements, and a compact icon rail for the application sidebar. Candidate principles P23 to P26 and candidate presets preset.workspace and preset.app-sidebar-rail travel as files in this folder; docs/WORKSPACE_PATTERN.md and the reference code (src/ui/workspaceGeometry.ts, src/ui/workspace.tsx, route #/workspace) are outside guidance/ and change no approved rule. It generalizes: any app with an image, canvas, preview, map or board as its main region hits the same layout problems. Open for the owner: ghost buttons (FB-0018) are deliberately not decided; whether P26 needs a check; the CHK-011 collector matches every aside; whether a quiet edge chevron is discoverable enough on a real touch device (FB-0037). CaissaTrainer Phase 2 extended this draft (FB-0020 to FB-0034): the size controls moved from the toolbar into a control rail attached to the region (FB-0020), optional tools and a duplicate view are closed by default and capped (FB-0021, FB-0022), the default is sized against panel minimums with the rail reserved on both sides (FB-0023), drawers are modal dialogs (FB-0024). Candidate amendments outside the workspace pattern are in candidate/amendments.md: tags and colour (AP-005, P06, CHK-005, FB-0025), equal surface check (FB-0028), editable text fields (FB-0026), toolbar density (FB-0027), honest toggles (FB-0034), repeated controls (FB-0030 to FB-0033), undefined class lint (FB-0029). Several are failures to apply approved guidance, not gaps (FB-0025, FB-0029, FB-0033, part of FB-0028); the proposal lists which. CaissaTrainer Phase 3 (FB-0035 to FB-0041, plus updates recorded on FB-0021, FB-0023, FB-0024, FB-0026, FB-0027 and FB-0034) revised the draft: hidden panels reserve no width and the board plus its open panels are centered as one group (replacing the equal reserve rule, FB-0036); panels are shown and hidden by quiet edge chevrons that report aria-expanded, with no toolbar toggle and no panel X (FB-0037); the optional left panel yields to a drawer before the layout restacks (COMFORT_MIN 400); a portrait window stacks when stacking gives a much bigger board; the default cap is 720 and fill 0.92; stacking is ordered by task (FB-0040); optional tools are a per module capability that never strands user data (FB-0041). Phase 3 also recorded redundant explanatory copy (FB-0035, FB-0038), classified as a failure to apply P04, P05, P09, P21, AP-005 and AP-010, with a drafted AP-010 clarification and an optional narrow check in amendments.md section I, and reconciled the Phase 2 editable field draft (FB-0026) so a save state is shown only when it communicates a condition. Session information (FB-0039) is an ambiguity, not drafted as a rule. Draft only: the owner decides everything, including whether to split this proposal. CaissaTrainer Phase 4 (FB-0042 to FB-0044, updates on FB-0020 and FB-0041): the control rail was refined from two floating transparent icons into one narrow rectangular column exactly as tall as the region with the options control on its top edge and the resize control on its bottom edge, measured from the region box (FB-0042; candidate wording inside P23, with an optional P11 clarification for the owner; classified as a guidance gap, not already covered by P11, whose approved text concerns indentation); a persistent contextual return control and its stacking order below modal layers (FB-0043, small gap); a temporary context carried by an opaque id (FB-0044, an integration note candidate with low confidence it is design guidance); progressive linking between two areas is merged into FB-0041 as mostly covered. Candidate wording is in candidate/amendments.md section K and is not policy. The React reference (src/ui/workspace.tsx, src/styles/workspace.css) and docs/WORKSPACE_PATTERN.md follow it, with a measured browser test (scripts/test-workspace-alignment.mjs) and 5 CSS and structure cases in scripts/test-workspace.mjs.

negative.description: Fixed-size central content: a 640px board or preview box. Too small on a large monitor, too large on a laptop, and the person cannot change it.
Storing a measurement as a preference: the window shrinks, the clamped size is saved, and the person's choice is lost for good.
negative.snippet:
const shown = Math.min(Math.max(size, 280), maxThatFits);
localStorage.setItem('size', String(shown));  /* P25: stores the clamp, not the choice */

negative.description: Panels that squeeze the primary region and vanish with no way back: a fixed 360px column on each side at every width, hidden by display:none on small screens.
negative.snippet: @media (max-width: 1000px) { .side { display: none; } }  /* P24: deleted, not yielded */

negative.description: Four size buttons in the page toolbar, far from the region they act on (FB-0020).
A category hue per ability repeated on every card, using the warning colour for one of them (FB-0025).
negative.snippet: .chip-calc { background: rgb(224 176 74 / .14); color: var(--warn); }  /* AP-005, P06, P04 */

negative.description: A drawer that sets focus on open but leaves the page behind it focusable (FB-0024).
negative.snippet: <aside role="dialog">...</aside>  /* no aria-modal, background not inert, Tab escapes */

negative.description: A second full size board next to the puzzle board, shown by default (FB-0022).
Panels toggled by two toolbar buttons named after the panels, each panel carrying an X (FB-0037).
An equal reserve column for a hidden panel: the region sits beside an empty void (FB-0036).
negative.snippet: grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) var(--ws-size) minmax(0, 1fr);  /* the empty side keeps its column; use [left track] [region + rail margin] [right track], tracks 0 when hidden */

negative.description: Redundant explanatory copy: a label repeating the panel title and a permanent save line (FB-0035).
A collapsible panel that is the only owner of a control the person needs to continue (FB-0037).
negative.snippet: <aside class="collapsible"><button>Next puzzle</button></aside>  /* put controls needed to continue in the strip or footer under the region */

negative.description: Controls floating beside the primary region with no container and arbitrary insets from its corners: they look detached from the region (FB-0042).
The same in the reference lab before the fix (FB-0042).
Positioning region controls from page coordinates instead of the region box (FB-0042).
negative.snippet: .region-tools { position: fixed; top: 96px; left: 1040px; }  /* breaks when the region resizes or the window changes; measure from the region */

positive.description: Reference route #/workspace at 1440px (Phase 3): the preview and the supporting panel are centered as one group, the optional Pages panel is closed behind its edge chevron and reserves no width, the size controls are the rail beside the preview.
At 1100px the supporting panel docks beside the preview, the application sidebar is the 56px rail, and the optional panel waits behind its edge chevron (P23, P24).

At 390px the workspace stacks in task order: the preview first at full width, its rail, the supporting information, then the optional Pages panel behind a disclosure row, 40px touch targets (P24, P18, FB-0040).
Geometry is a pure function and the stored size is only an input.
positive.snippet:
const g = computeWorkspace({ width, height, padding: 16, gap: 16, chromeY, left, right, leftOpen, rightOpen, preferred: prefs.size /* null = responsive default */ });
prefs.setSize(pickedSize); /* the pick, never g.size */

positive.description: The same slice after Phase 2: duplicate board collapsed by default, capped at 240px, grouped options menu (FB-0022, FB-0027).
Rail options menu open on the reference route: a menu button with the four discrete actions.
Taxonomy chips removed, ability named in one plain line on the overview (FB-0025).

Both panels open at 1440: a quiet Pages surface on the left, the preview, and the flat Properties panel with no heading or card on the right; chevrons on both outer edges point the way each panel will move (FB-0036, FB-0037).
Both panels hidden: no empty columns, the preview is centered on its own and each edge chevron says Show (FB-0036).
The optional panel as a modal drawer when it cannot dock beside a comfortable preview (COMFORT_MIN 400), closed by a back chevron, not an X (FB-0023 update, FB-0024, FB-0037).
Portrait tablet at 820 stacks because that gives a much bigger preview; the optional panel is a disclosure row (FB-0023 update).
Redundant copy removed: the Notes panel keeps its heading, an accessible name and a prompt while empty; no repeated label, no permanent save line (FB-0035).
Save state only when it is news: a status only while a request is in flight and a failure with a retry, nothing at rest.
positive.snippet:
{saving ? 'Saving...' : ''}
{failed &&
Could not save
} /* nothing when idle or saved (FB-0035) */

positive.description: Panel toggle as an edge chevron that reports what is on screen.
positive.snippet: <button type="button" class="ws-edge ws-edge-left" data-ws-toggle="left" aria-expanded={shown} aria-label={shown ? 'Hide Pages' : 'Show Pages'}>...chevron...</button>  /* no toolbar toggle, no X (FB-0037) */

positive.description: One narrow rectangular column exactly as tall as the board, options on the top edge, resize on the bottom edge, one alignment (CaissaTrainer Phase 4, e2e measured 122 to 674 against 122 to 674, 8px gap) (FB-0042).
The reference lab after the fix, measured by scripts/test-workspace-alignment.mjs (rail 102 to 790 against region 102 to 790 at 1440x900).
Region controls measured from the region box.
positive.snippet:
.region { position: relative; }
.region-rail { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: calc(100% + 8px); width: 32px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; background: var(--s2); }

positive.description: Stacked: a compact row under the board aligned to its right edge, 40px targets (FB-0042).

validation.notes: Re-run by claude-agent after the Phase 3 update (edge chevron toggles, hidden panels reserve no width, drawer before restack, portrait stacking, cap 720 and fill 0.92, new issues FB-0035 to FB-0041, AP-010 clarification drafted): result no-regressions on the 12 approved references at 1440 and 390, tap test pass (940 elements, 0 undersized, 0 tap mismatches on the 12 applications), desktop layout comparison changed for trading only (31 elements at 1440, 59 at 1100 in this run, 82 and 82 in a second run: the count varies between runs because the trading reference shows live ticking data, the same pre-existing time dependent behaviour recorded in the Phase 2 run; trading does not use the workspace pattern; the other 11 applications show 0 changed). No candidate check is implemented, so no check outcome can change. #/workspace tap test (node scripts/test-tap-targets.mjs --apps workspace, with new scenarios for the optional panel and the rail menu): 390x844 24 tested, 820x1180 23 tested, 0 undersized, 0 tap mismatches; the edge chevron measured 32x64 effective when it hugged the screen edge and 40x64 after it was moved 8px in (found and fixed during this run; checked at 1100x700 with a touch context). npm run test:workspace: 48 pass (includes parity with CaissaTrainer workspaceLayout.ts). Re-run by claude-agent after the Phase 4 update (rail column as tall as the region, FB-0042 to FB-0044): npm run regression with --with-tap --with-layout: result no-regressions on the 12 approved references at 1440 and 390, tap test pass (940 elements, 0 undersized, 0 tap mismatches), desktop layout comparison changed for trading only (31 elements at 1440, 0 at 1100 in this run; trading shows live ticking data, the same pre-existing time dependent behaviour recorded earlier, and does not use the workspace pattern; the other 11 applications show 0 changed). No candidate check is implemented, so no check outcome can change. #/workspace tap test (node scripts/test-tap-targets.mjs --apps workspace): 390x844 24 tested, 820x1180 23 tested, 0 undersized, 0 tap mismatches (the 1100x700 run of that script stops in its drawer scenario, which needs the mobile navigation button and does not exist at that width; unrelated to this change). New measured test scripts/test-workspace-alignment.mjs: 24 of 24 pass at 1440x900, 1100x700 and 390x844 (it fails 8 of 24 on the previous CSS). npm run test:workspace: 53 pass. npm run validate, npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build pass. Not an approval.

existingApplications.note: Existing applications are not changed. The 12 prototypes render identically (npm run test:desktop-layout). CaissaTrainer keeps guidance 0.1.0 in its summa-ui.usage.json until the owner approves a release and requests an update. AppShell gained an optional compact prop that is off by default.
